_about: Crazyflie 2.0 vehicle parameters for scripts/quad.py and app/sim/quad.js. Every entry: value, unit, source (URL + page), quote (verbatim, from the source opened 2026-10-11), kind = measured | derived | assumption. Edit here only; quad.py regenerates app/sim/vehicle_params.js from this file.

mass.note: Menagerie README: 'Set the inertial properties to values obtained from the datasheet and MIT's system identification'. Förster 2015 App. A measured 28.0 g on his unit; we keep the Menagerie value so MuJoCo and numpy share one mass.

Ixx.source: Landry 2015, MIT MEng thesis, Table 4.1 (PDF p. 39), https://groups.csail.mit.edu/robotics-center/public_papers/Landry15.pdf ; same value in Menagerie cf2.xml
Ixx.quote: Ixx 2.3951 · 10−5 kg · m2 ... Table 4.1: The parameters identified with our approach for the Crazyflie.

arm_length.source: Förster 2015, 'System Identification of the Crazyflie 2.0 Nano Quadrocopter', BSc thesis, ETH Zurich (IDSC-RD-MDH-04), pp. 17 and 20, doi:10.3929/ethz-b-000214143 ; Crazyflie firmware platform_defaults_cf2.h @ f6e0f0a, https://github.com/bitcraze/crazyflie-firmware/blob/f6e0f0a3b526861328caf3296a7ecf00bb915d39/src/platform/interface/platform_defaults_cf2.h
arm_length.quote: Förster p.20: 'Assume that dCF is the distance between two opposite motor axes of the Crazyflie.' p.17: '(dCF = 0.092 m)'. Firmware: '#define ARM_LENGTH  0.046f' under '// m'
arm_length.note: Centre to motor axis = dCF/2. Roll/pitch moment arm in the X layout = arm_length/sqrt(2) = 0.0325 m (firmware: 'const float arm = 0.707106781f * ARM_LENGTH;').

thrust_a2.source: Förster 2015, Appendix A 'Overview Results' p. 57 (and Sec. 3.3.1 p. 27)

cmd_max.quote: Send a setpoint from the interval [0, 65535] to the motor

rotor_b1.source: Förster 2015, Appendix A p. 57 and Sec. 3.3.2 p. 28 (second series, recommended)
rotor_b1.quote: Input Command → Rotor Angular Velocity θi = 0.04076521 · cmdi + 380.8359
rotor_b1.note: Units rad/s per Fig. 3.10 axis 'Angular velocity [rad/s]'. Used only for the drag model (sum of rotor speeds).

thrust2torque.unit: m (N m of drag torque per N of thrust)
thrust2torque.source: Förster 2015, Appendix A p. 57 and Sec. 3.3.3 p. 29 ; identical to firmware platform_defaults.h THRUST2TORQUE
thrust2torque.quote: Thrust → Torque τi = 0.005964552 · fi + 1.563383 · 10−5 ; firmware: '#define THRUST2TORQUE   0.005964552f'
thrust2torque.note: The constant 1.563e-5 N m cancels in the yaw sum (two CW, two CCW rotors) and is omitted.

motor_pole.source: Förster 2015, Sec. 3.4.4 eq. (3.16)-(3.17) p. 34 and Appendix A p. 57
motor_pole.quote: H2(z) = 7.2345374 · 10−8 / (1 − 0.9695404 · z−1) ... it is recommended to use the second transfer function: H(z) = H2(z).

motor_pole_dt.quote: it starts generating the input sequence and commanding it to the specified motor(s) with a frequency of 500 Hz
motor_pole_dt.note: Cross-check: the thesis says l > 200 with N = 8000 corresponds to 12.5 Hz; 2*pi*200/8000 rad/sample * 500 Hz / (2*pi) = 12.5 Hz, so the z-domain sample rate is 500 Hz.

motor_tau.note: Förster p. 35: latency was not compensated ('currently the latency of the signals is completely omitted'), so this first-order lag lumps motor dynamics and some latency.

f_max.source: derived: thrust map at cmd = 65535 (Förster App. A); consistent with Förster Sec. 3.3.1 p. 27
f_max.quote: the maximum thrust that can be produced by one motor was determined to be approximately 0.15 N
f_max.note: Thrust saturation. Hover needs mass*g/4 = 0.0662 N per motor (41% of f_max).

kaero_xy.source: Förster 2015, Appendix A p. 57 'Drag Coefficients, Simple Model' (Sec. 4 p. 39 for the model)
kaero_xy.quote: fa = Kaero θ̇Σ R−1 ẋ ; Kaero = diag(−9.1785 · 10−7, −9.1785 · 10−7, −10.311 · 10−7) kg · rad−1 ; θ̇Σ = Σ|θ̇i| the sum of the angular velocities of all rotors
kaero_xy.note: We use air-relative velocity (ẋ - wind) in place of ẋ; Förster's model assumes still air. Linear drag only; ~6.8e-3 N per m/s at hover rotor speed.

g.source: MuJoCo default gravity (0 0 -9.81), used so the MuJoCo check shares it

layout.frame: Body frame x forward, y left, z up (FLU, as in the Crazyflie firmware). World ENU: x east, y north, z up. quat (w,x,y,z) rotates body to world.
layout.motors: M1 front-right (+x,-y), M2 back-right (-x,-y), M3 back-left (-x,+y), M4 front-left (+x,+y), each at arm_length/sqrt(2) along x and y. M1, M3 spin counter-clockwise seen from above; M2, M4 clockwise. Yaw torque on the body = thrust2torque * (-f1 + f2 - f3 + f4).
layout.source: Crazyflie firmware power_distribution_quadrotor.c @ f6e0f0a, powerDistributionForceTorque: 'motorForces[0] = thrustPart - rollPart - pitchPart - yawPart; motorForces[1] = thrustPart - rollPart + pitchPart + yawPart; motorForces[2] = thrustPart + rollPart + pitchPart - yawPart; motorForces[3] = thrustPart + rollPart - pitchPart + yawPart;' (signs imply the positions and spins above for an FLU body frame), https://github.com/bitcraze/crazyflie-firmware/blob/f6e0f0a3b526861328caf3296a7ecf00bb915d39/src/modules/src/power_distribution_quadrotor.c

controller.structure: Cascade PID as in the Crazyflie firmware: 'The firmware employs distinct PID controllers for each control level: position, velocity, attitude, and attitude rate.' 'The output of each controller feeds into the input of the next, lower level controller, forming a cascaded PID structure.' (https://www.bitcraze.io/documentation/repository/crazyflie-firmware/master/functional-areas/sensor-to-control/controllers/). Ours: altitude P -> vertical-velocity PI; horizontal velocity PI -> tilt; attitude P -> body-rate PID -> force/torque mixer -> thrust cap as in firmware powerDistributionCap (subtract the excess over f_max from all motors, then clip at 0). All loops run every physics step (500 Hz); the firmware runs position/velocity at 100 Hz.
controller.gains: Our own SI gains (firmware gains are in PWM/degree units and are not reused); listed in scripts/quad.py GAINS and reported in results/quad_selfcheck.json.

dryden.model: MIL-F-8785C low-altitude Dryden, as documented by MathWorks Aerospace Blockset 'Dryden Wind Turbulence Model (Continuous)', https://www.mathworks.com/help/aeroblks/drydenwindturbulencemodelcontinuous.html
dryden.quote: Lw = h, Lu = Lv = h/(0.177+0.000823h)^1.2 ; σw = 0.1 W20, σu/σw = σv/σw = 1/(0.177+0.000823h)^0.4 ; W20 '15 knots in light turbulence, 30 knots in moderate turbulence, and 45 knots for severe turbulence' ; Hu(s) = σu sqrt(2Lu/(πV)) · 1/(1+(Lu/V)s) ; Hv(s) = σv sqrt(Lv/(πV)) · (1+(√3Lv/V)s)/(1+(Lv/V)s)^2 ; Hw likewise with Lw, σw
dryden.assumptions: h in ft inside the formulas, clamped to >= 10 ft (the low-altitude formulas give L -> 0 at the ground); V = 2 m/s nominal airspeed (a hovering drone has no meaningful V; a frozen-turbulence field convected at 2 m/s); turbulence components u, v, w are applied along world x, y, z (not rotated into the mean-wind direction); white noise is a zero-order-held N(0,1) sequence scaled to two-sided PSD π so that each shaping filter's output variance equals σ².
